title: Evaluation of Test Items Efficacy in Promoting Stroke Rehabilitation in the Rat Stroke Model
author: Aharon Levy
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf69jrh6

steps.title: Acclimate and identify animals
steps.instruction: Acclimate male Sprague‑Dawley rats (~3 months, ~300 g) for at least five days; identify each animal by three‑position ear notching and cage cards, ensuring group body‑weight range is within ±20 % of the mean.

steps.title: House and maintain animal environment
steps.instruction: House rats under NIH/AAALAC guidelines with ad‑libitum commercial rodent diet and acidified water; keep cages in a HEPA‑filtered (F6/6) room with ≥15 air changes / h, temperature 20–24 °C, humidity 30–70 %, 12 h light/12 h dark cycle.

steps.title: Provide analgesia before surgery
steps.instruction: Administer analgesia before the first surgery and then on the end of Day 1 and each of the next four days: Buprenorphine 0.05–0.10 mg kg⁻¹ SC every 6–12 h **or** Carprofen 5 mg kg⁻¹ SC every 12–24 h.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia for surgery
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 4 % isoflurane in 70 % N₂O + 30 % O₂; maintain with 1.5–2 % isoflurane on a heating pad throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Perform transient MCA occlusion (t‑MCAO)
steps.instruction: Expose the right common carotid artery (CCA) via a midline neck incision, dissect it free from nerves and fascia, isolate and coagulate occipital branches of the external carotid artery (ECA), then coagulate and divide distal ECA, lingual and maxillary branches. Isolate the internal carotid artery (ICA), separate it from the vagus nerve, and ligate the pterygopalatine artery with a 5‑0 nylon suture (SMI, Belgium). Tie a loose 4‑0 silk suture around the ECA stump, insert a 4 cm length of 4‑0 monofilament nylon (tip blunted by flame, coated with polylysine) through the proximal ECA into the ICA and circle of Willis to occlude the MCA. Close the wound, return the rat to its cage, and keep on a heating pad until awake. After 1.5 h, re‑anesthetize, withdraw the monofilament to allow reperfusion, close the wound again, and return the animal to its cage.

steps.title: Post‑operative monitoring and recovery
steps.instruction: Keep the animal on a heating pad until fully awake; observe the rat frequently on Day 1 and at least once daily thereafter, recording any signs of morbidity, mortality, or humane‑endpoint criteria (moribund condition, severe pain, distress, or >20 % body‑weight loss).

steps.title: Baseline behavioral assessments
steps.instruction: Before surgery, perform the following tests on each rat: Limb Placing (fore‑ and hind‑limb, scoring 0–12 forelimb, 0–6 hindlimb), Stepping Test (count adjusting steps while moving the rat sideways 85 cm in ~5 s for each forelimb, forehand and backhand), Body Swing Test (hold rat 1 in from tail, elevate 1 in above table, record 20 swings, calculate % rightward swings), and Modified Neurological Severity Score (mNSS, total 0–18). Record all scores.

steps.title: Day 2 mNSS and inclusion
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours after reperfusion (Day 2), assess each rat with the modified Neurological Severity Score (mNSS). Include only animals with a score ≥ 10 in the study; exclude all others.

steps.title: Randomize to treatment groups
steps.instruction: Allocate rats to vehicle or test‑item groups based on their Day 2 mNSS to achieve balanced performance distribution across groups.

steps.title: Administer test item or vehicle
steps.instruction: Begin treatment on Day 2 or Day 3 as dictated by the study drug; follow the dosing schedule and duration specified in Table 1 (e.g., vehicle or low/mid/high dose for 25 days, with a final cohort of at least 15 rats per group).

steps.title: Monitor body weight
steps.instruction: Measure each rat’s body weight three times per week throughout the study.

steps.title: Observe mortality and humane endpoints
steps.instruction: Check all animals twice daily for signs of morbidity, mortality, or humane‑endpoint criteria; euthanize moribund or severely distressed animals and record time of death precisely.

steps.title: End‑of‑study behavioral assessments
steps.instruction: At the study’s conclusion, repeat the Limb Placing, Stepping, Body Swing, and mNSS tests on all surviving rats, ensuring the investigator is blinded to treatment assignment.

steps.title: Sacrifice and harvest brains
steps.instruction: Euthanize all rats by CO₂ inhalation, perform routine perfusion, and harvest brains for downstream analysis.
